events.title: German Cabinet Approves Strategic Gas Reserve For Crises
events.summary: The German cabinet on 11 November approved plans for a new strategic gas reserve to prepare for sabotage or attacks on energy infrastructure. The reserve is to hold 24 terawatt-hours of additional physical gas, enough to secure supply for 30 days if deliveries fail completely, and is to be built up by Trading Hub Europe from 2027. It could be released only after the Federal Network Agency declares an emergency over a threatened gas shortage, and the government estimates the levy will cost households about four to seven euros a year.

events.title: Hundreds Of Thousands Join Metal Industry Warning Strikes
events.summary: Workers in Germany's metal and electrical industries began warning strikes on 1 November, after the peace obligation in the IG Metall pay talks expired. The union said more than 413,000 employees had joined strikes and rallies by 6 November. IG Metall is seeking a 5 percent pay rise, while employers have offered 1.3 percent from July 2028.

events.title: Youth-Led Protests Turn To Rioting And Looting In German Cities
events.summary: Youth-led "Gen Z regelt" demonstrations for education, health and affordable living took place in cities across Germany on 31 October. The marches were largely peaceful during the day, but rioting broke out after dark in cities including Frankfurt, Cologne, Hamburg and Berlin. In Frankfurt, shops were looted and a gun shop was attacked; police said they seized two weapons there. Organisers distanced themselves from the violence.

events.title: Fire Destroys Hitler's Former Eagle's Nest Retreat In Bavaria
events.summary: A fire engulfed the Kehlsteinhaus, the mountain building near Berchtesgaden known as Hitler's Eagle's Nest, on 23 October. No injuries were reported. Police detained a 33-year-old man; prosecutors said he showed signs of mental illness but that they would also examine a possible political motive. German media reported that investigators suspected arson.

events.title: Suspected Russian Spy Arrested In Brandenburg
events.summary: Federal Criminal Police officers arrested a Ukrainian national in the Oder-Spree district of Brandenburg on 22 October on suspicion of working for a Russian intelligence service, the Federal Prosecutor's Office said. Prosecutors allege he gathered information on the production of armoured vehicles, ammunition and explosives, and on military sites securing NATO's eastern flank. The case followed information from Germany's domestic intelligence agency.

events.title: Court Jails Two Men Over Iran-Directed Plot Against Jewish Leaders
events.summary: A court in Hamburg on 15 October sentenced a Danish national to eight and a half years and an Afghan national to four and a half years in prison over a plot steered by Iran's intelligence service against Jewish and pro-Israel figures in Germany. The targets included Josef Schuster, president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, and Volker Beck, head of the German-Israeli Society. Iran denied any role.
